conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the unit
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the class will spend 'the next 26 lessons' solving the mystery, but the sequence has only 13 lessons (Lesson 13 is the final consolidation, Lesson 9 previews 'Lessons 10 through 13').

conflicts.fact: How many lessons since the start
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says 'Seven lessons ago we asked...' (should be six); Lesson 13 says 'twelve lessons' of investigation, Lesson 10 says 'nine lessons' of evidence/'10 lessons of evidence' in the same lesson.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbers of earlier content / which lesson taught Lewis structure of H2O and covalent bonding
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says learners draw the Lewis structure of H₂O 'revisiting Lesson 3' and graphite hexagons 'the covalent bonds you know from Lesson 2', but ionic bonding is Lesson 3, and covalent/Lewis structures were Lesson 4 (Lesson 2 was valence electrons). Lesson 10 says delocalised electrons were 'Lesson 7' though taught in Lessons 4/6.

conflicts.fact: Bond types and metallic bonding timing
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says learners know 'five types of bonding or force: ionic, covalent, dative covalent, metallic, and now intermolecular forces', but metallic bonding is not taught until Lesson 6.

Lesson 11 says the bulb-and-wire experiment was 'last week' and the graphite/diamond conductivity result was from 'Lesson 8' (where only graphite powder was tested, no diamond); the graphite-vs-diamond conductivity demo was Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: Whether diamond/graphite conductivity data was collected
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 tests five substances (graphite included, no diamond) and shows graphite conducting; Lesson 9 says the four substances tested were NaCl, sugar, SiO2, aluminium and that graphite 'if it was tested' may or may not appear, contradicting Lesson 8's recorded graphite result. Lesson 9 also treats it as '40-minute period' whereas Lessons 3, 5, 10 are 80 minutes.

Lesson 7 predicts for four unknowns (NaCl, sugar, SiO2, aluminium) plus diamond and graphite; Lesson 8 tests five substances with graphite in place of testing diamond and says it covers 'four other substances' beyond the carbon pair in teacher script while the table lists five including graphite.

Lessons 1/4/6 say delocalised electron within each layer; Lessons 11 and 13 say 'between layers' (Lesson 13: 'fourth electron delocalised between the layers'), while Lesson 12 says 'across the layer'.
Lesson 1 uses a 6V battery-bulb tester; Lesson 6 uses a 9V battery with LED bulb.

conflicts.fact: Cl- electron configuration description / Na+ shell
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says Na⁺ has 'empty outer shell' in dot-and-cross while also saying Na has full outer shell (2,8) after transfer; minor inconsistency in wording.

Lesson 10 says SiO₂ is transparent and used in glassmaking and as a hard substance; Lesson 12 says SiO₂ gives 'extreme hardness'; Lesson 9 groups SiO2 sand as non-conducting giant covalent, consistent, but Lesson 13 lists graphite among 'giant covalent structures extremely hard' (diamond, SiO2) while graphite is soft.
